title: Introduce Reservoir Throttle Arbiter and Lag Mitigator for Dedicated Fleets
author: Aisha Mehta
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally observe short-lived headroom starvation when many mid-sized tenants burst concurrently. The existing admission path provides per-tenant soft reservations and a simple first-fit burst allowance, but we see tail latency spikes and over-eager decommits under correlated bursts. This PR introduces a reservoir-based throttle arbiter that mediates burst grants across tenant groups and a lag mitigation controller that reduces reactive provisioning churn.

What this change does (summary): 1) reservoir/arbiter: adds a lightweight in-memory reservoir that tracks short-term burst budget across the fleet and issues proportional ephemeral grants based on recent utilization fingerprints and configured fairness weights; 2) lag mitigator: smooths autoscaler signals by detecting provisioning lag (nodes pending/booting) and temporarily biasing admission towards conservative allocations until capacity stabilizes; 3) telemetry: exports new metrics and sketches to diagnose burst contention and reservoir depletion; 4) safety: falls back to current behavior on misconfiguration and supports an opt-in feature-flag.

Design notes: - Reservoir state is sharded per-pool to avoid global lock contention. Each shard maintains a leaky-bucket style token pool with time-decay replenishment calibrated by pool commit size and historical burst frequency. - The arbiter issues ephemeral grants bounded by tenant-configured max-burst and global per-pool headroom. Grants are revocable and include a best-effort TTL. - The lag mitigator computes a provisioning gap metric (pending_nodes_weighted - expected_boot_capacity) and applies a sigmoid dampening to scale down ephemeral grants when gap > threshold. Dampening parameters are tunable via the autoscaler config map.

Checklist: - [x] Core reservoir implementation with unit tests and deterministic time control
- [x] Lag mitigator controller and integration tests (simulated provisioning delay)
- [x] Telemetry hooks (metrics, HDR sketches) + Grafana dashboard draft
- [x] Feature flag gate + config map defaults preserved
- [x] E2E scenario reproducing correlated two-tenant bursts
- [x] Docs: operator runbook and tuning guide

Why this is safe: The arbiter is opt-in per-pool and defaults to an inert mode that mirrors existing admission behavior. All grants are bounded and revocable; if the controller process crashes the system reverts to existing admission. We included a kill-switch and health-checks that force-drain the reservoir on mismatch.

How tested: Unit and integration tests included. The e2e suite simulates fleets with varying boot latencies (0s-120s) and shows 40-55% reduction in tail-99 latency for short bursts across our synthetic workload. Perf bench harness run on internal bench cluster (bench-01) shows median token allocation latency unchanged, and sustained throughput within 2% of baseline.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on staging pools (opt-in) for 48h 2) Monitor reservoir_depletion_rate, provisioning_gap, tenant_throttle_events and tail latency 3) Gradual ramp to 30% production pools with daily checkpoints 4) Full rollout if no regressions after 7 days.

Related: ENG-1829 (throughput guarantees), ENG-1974 (eviction smoothing), SUP-412 (customer incident that motivated lag mitigator).

review_comments:
Jonas Park (2025-01-13): Nice approach. Two requests: (1) add a short doc comment on the mathematical properties of the replenishment decay so on-call can reason about parameters; (2) prefer context-aware cancellations in the arbiter grant path to avoid leaks. See inline.

Author (Aisha): Added comment and switched to context-aware grant workflows in the latest commit (b4c5d22).

Miguel Alvarez (2025-01-15): Can we add a safety unit test for controller crash + restart so we verify we don't double-credit the reservoir? Also the e2e seemed flaky once with a delayed API—I added a repro in the CI logs.

Author: Added TestReservoirIdempotentRecovery and extended e2e harness to tolerate API delay up to 5s. Fixed race in shard init. (commit 9f3a2d1).

Priya Singh (2025-01-17): From an SRE perspective, please expose an alert recipe for persistent reservoir_depletion_rate > 0.8 over a 10m window and add playbook steps. Docs updated.

Author: Added alert recommendations to docs and included grafana dashboard snapshot.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in reservoir-based burst arbiter and provisioning lag mitigator for Dedicated fleets. Adds telemetry for reservoir depletion and provisioning gap. Operators can tune decay and dampening parameters via the autoscaler config map.
notes_for_oncall: If tail latency increases after enabling for a pool: 1) check reservoir_depletion_rate and provisioning_gap metrics; 2) toggle feature flag to revert to baseline admission; 3) consult docs/ops/dedicated/lag-mitigation.md for tuning parameters and playbook steps; 4) run TestReservoirIdempotentRecovery locally to reproduce restart semantics.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: miscalibrated decay/dampening could starve legitimate bursts or over-issue grants. Mitigation: defaults are conservative, feature is opt-in, grants bounded and revocable, metrics and alerting added, rollback via feature flag. Runbook included.
e2e_results_summary: Synthetic two-tenant correlated burst test: baseline tail-99 = 1.8s, with arbiter tail-99 = 0.95s (median of 5 runs); provisioning-gap > 0 scenario reduced oscillation in autoscaler decisions and reduced unnecessary decommits by ~33%.
additional_context: This PR complements existing autoscaler work by focusing on short-term burst fairness and reducing reactive provisioning churn. It is intentionally orthogonal to long-window capacity planners; the reservoir only affects ephemeral granting and does not change reserved capacity commitments.
